reader.requirement: After RELEASE the released record is no longer available in the record area (contents undefined) unless the SD is named in a SAME RECORD AREA clause; then the record stays in the area and is also available as a record of every other file in that clause (an implicit redefinition aligned leftmost, §1985:XI.2.5.4 GR1), for every record description of the SD, fixed or variable, and for RELEASE with or without FROM.

edition-consulted.switches: rangeFailsStatement = DialectLevel < 2002: at 85 a varying record outside the record range makes the RELEASE unsuccessful (§1985:VII.3.8.4 GR10); later editions release it. The 'also available' store is gated on that success

reader.edition-search: grep for Edition/DialectLevel/DialectBehavior in SortEmitter.EmitRelease, SequentialIoEmitter's released-record helpers and FileControlBinder.IoControl's SAME RECORD AREA link: none; the only edition test on the RELEASE path is SortBinder.BindRelease's rangeFailsStatement, which governs an out-of-range varying release, not this rule.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the shared area is one redefinition (LinkSameRecordArea) at every edition; the store for out-of-line records cannot arise at 85 (no DYNAMIC LENGTH or pointer records)

reader.notes: LinkSameRecordArea makes each peer's record area a redefinition of the anchor's, so character-window records share one backing and the released bytes are visible through every peer with no emitted store; BeginReleasedRecord/EmitReleasedRecordAlsoAvailable add a store only for out-of-line records, which 85 cannot declare. The 'no longer available' half leaves content undefined, so keeping the bytes conforms.

refuter.evidence: Probe E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-201/src/r1.cob (run r1-002, --std 85): SAME RECORD AREA FOR S1 S2 IXF OUTF (two SDs, an INDEXED file and a sequential file, both open OUTPUT). After RELEASE S1-REC the second SD's record shows the bytes ('S2=[KKKABCD0123]'); the indexed record's COMP field equals a WORKING-STORAGE REDEFINES of the same four bytes ('BIN SAME'), its display numeric computes from them ('IX-NUM+1=00124'), and WRITE IX-REC / WRITE OUT-REC with no MOVE write the released record (read back: 'IX READ 00 NUM=0123', 'OUTF REC1=[JJJWXYZ0007]'); RELEASE FROM a WS item shows in OUT-REC ('FROM S2 -> OUT=[AAA2-------]', REC2). All three reach the sort in order. A first run (r1-001) showed 1985's AT END / INVALID KEY syntax rules enforced. LinkSameRecordArea's single redefinition holds for typed native fields too. cite.py: OK §1985:XI.4.2.4 GR2 'is no longer available in the record area unless'; OK §1985:XI.2.5.4 GR1 'The SAME RECORD AREA clause specifies that two or more files'.
